Experts advise against using concentrated UV light on the body to prevent or treat coronavirus because the intensities required to inactivate viruses are much higher than sunlight and can damage skin, so it should be avoided [1]. While UVC light can inactivate viruses on surfaces and is used in controlled settings (e.g., hospitals, germ-zapping robots), its application is technical, dose-dependent, and still being studied for complex items like PPE; it is not a personal preventive measure [1]. Public health agencies such as WHO and CDC do not list sunlight or UV exposure as recommended prevention methods for COVID-19 [0].  [1]
